Title: Ship Construction & Refit
Description: Learn how to refit and expand a modular Subspace vessel using structural elements, authored modules and semantic attachment points.

Steps.Title: Persistent Ships
Steps.Message: Your vessel is a persistent assembly. Hull structure, modules, cargo, damage, paint and installed systems remain with the same ship when you land, dock, travel and save.

Steps.Title: Hangar Shipyard
Steps.Message: Dock at a compatible hangar, berth or drydock to enter the in-game Shipyard. The Shipyard modifies the actual vessel being serviced rather than creating a separate editor-only copy.

Steps.Title: Construction Vocabulary
Steps.Message: Ships combine structural/parametric elements with authored modules. Semantic sockets and attachment faces govern valid connections. Typical systems include command, hull/armor, engines, maneuvering thrusters, power, shields, cargo, sensors, weapons, interiors and support equipment.

Steps.Title: Engineering Consequences
Steps.Message: Every addition can affect mass, center of mass, thrust authority, power demand, cooling, fuel, cargo, protection, weapon arcs, interior clearance and atmospheric capability. The validator reports blocking problems before a refit is committed.

Steps.Title: Materials and Manufacturing
Steps.Message: Material and module quality come from Subspace resources, manufacturing capability, provenance and condition. Current progression is not tied to the retired donor material-tier ladder.

Steps.Title: Construction Complete
Steps.Message: Use the Shipyard to repair, refit, paint and expand the same vessel you later board and undock. Developer authoring in Ember will eventually use the same canonical assembly schemas and validators.
